mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea registry system
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille): notarize at a Korean notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Path B (Consular Legalization for non-Hague destinations): notarize, then legalize at the Korean consular office of the destination jurisdiction. Choose only Path A or Path B; never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Existence and Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and the competent District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille): notarize, then Apostille at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Path B (Consular Legalization): notarize, then legalize through the Korean consular mission of the destination country. The two paths are mutually exclusive and cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Licensing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Intended sole quota holder or incorporator of the Yuhan Hoesa; certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille): notarization followed by Apostille at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Path B (Consular Legalization): notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate for the destination jurisdiction; use only one path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Initial Version for Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa incorporators; attested by drafting counsel and Korean notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille): notarize and apostille through the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Path B (Consular Legalization): notarize and legalize before the Korean consulate with jurisdiction over the destination country; the paths are parallel alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Escrow Bank Account Opening Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank designated for the factoring escrow and SWIFT wire payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille): bank officer countersignature, notarization, then Apostille at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Path B (Consular Legalization): bank officer countersignature, notarization, then Korean consular legalization for non-Hague destination; do not add Apostille where consular legalization is used.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and on a continuous 24/7 basis against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Korea FIU domestic watchlists, the Republic of Korea sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and FATF-identified increased-risk jurisdictions. Every beneficial owner, signatory, intermediary, counterparty, and factor client must be screened before any share registration, wire transfer, or factoring facility approval. PEP identification must use at least two independent data sources, including Korean government gazettes, regulatory enforcement records, and international PEP databases. Adverse hits require enhanced due diligence, adverse media investigation, and a 48-hour escalation to the AML compliance committee. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under suspicious transaction reporting rules. Factoring counterparties located in non-Hague countries must supply consular-legalized corporate evidence and are assigned enhanced geographic risk scoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (i-reg.go.kr) and the National Tax Service Hometax Business Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul or in Hangul-compatible Korean characters, and it must include the legal-form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. Foreign-script names are supplementary and cannot be used as the sole registered name unless lawfully transliterated into Korean. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive principal word in Korean; (2) the business purpose description; (3) the place of registered office; and (4) the mandatory legal-form suffix. Chinese-character names are permitted only as auxiliary entries accompanied by Korean phonetic notation; pure English names are not independently registrable as the statutory trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the registration court, the applicant has the right to file a request for correction or an administrative appeal within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice, citing Article 35 of the Korean Commercial Registration Rules. The appeal must be submitted to the competent district court that processed the name clearance, with an amended trade name and any consent letters or ministerial pre-approvals needed for sensitive tokens. If the district court denies the request, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal to the Seoul High Court within 30 days. Counsel should attach the search report, proposed Articles of Association, and a written explanation of the unique transliteration and business purpose to minimize further rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected for this ISIC 6492 factoring entity. Korea's Commercial Act and the Specialized Credit Financial Business Act require a fixed place of business where the factor maintains original contracts, statutory ledgers, IT infrastructure, employee presence, and regulatory records. Korean banks and the Financial Services Commission will not accept a provider mailbox as a registered office for a factoring company. A shared office or business center may pass only if backed by a dedicated lease, on-site signage, local management, actual employee attendance, and verifiable operational substance. For non-licensed holding companies, virtual offices may be tolerated, but this trade finance factoring scope demands a physical lease and demonstrable commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for regulatory inspection: (a) registered office nameplate and signage; (b) lease agreement with at least a 12-month term; (c) local employees or an authorized registered agent physically accessible; (d) original factoring agreements, invoices, and statutory ledgers; (e) SANs and unrelated-transaction monitoring records; (f) AML/CFT compliance manual; (g) data processing and escrow account infrastructure; (h) bank statements and remittance records. Quantified risk for a new factoring Yuhan Hoesa in the first 24 months is 55% for a municipal tax office inspection, 62% for Financial Services Commission and Korea FIU compliance inspection, and 35% for an unscheduled bank or knowledge-broker site visit. If a virtual office is substituted, the inspection probability rises above 85% and exposes the entity to administrative penalties and licensing revocation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Book IV on Limited Liability Companies (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-1 through 287-44; Specialized Credit Finance Business Act, Article 3 and its Enforcement Decree; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 6-2; Value-Added Tax Act, Article 8
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, operating under the Court Registry Office system of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Commercial Registration Act, evidenced by the Certificate of Registered Matters and the Certificate of Company Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; however, the amount of capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid by each member before the registration application is filed, and the paid-in contribution must be deposited into a dedicated capital contribution bank account opened in the proposed corporate name. For non-resident investors, inward remittance must be made through a Korean foreign exchange bank and the bank certificate of deposit or certificate of contribution must be attached to the registration dossier. There is no statutory escrow release arrangement under Korean company law, but the contribution account is treated as blocked for company formation purposes and none of the funds may be withdrawn until the Court Registry issues the Certificate of Company Registration. If the entity will operate factoring under the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act, the Financial Services Commission requires the registered company to maintain real paid-in capital and own capital not lower than the thresholds prescribed by the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and those capital tests must be satisfied before factoring operations lawfully commence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING OF THE INCORPORATORS AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (YUHAN HOESA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) HELD IN SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS]. The incorporators, representing one hundred percent of the subscribed capital, and the duly appointed initial directors, composing a full quorum, unanimously adopted the following resolutions, each to be effective immediately and conditioned only upon completion of statutory registration under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act, where applicable. 1. Subscription and Share Capital. RESOLVED, that the authorized and issued share capital of the Company shall be as stated in the Articles of Incorporation; that each member's contribution is subscribed in full; and that no member shall be released from any unpaid contribution obligation. The Representative Director is authorized to open a capital contribution bank account, receive contributions of not less than the amount resolved, and obtain the bank certificate of contribution for filing with the competent Court Registry. 2. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be located at [Registered Office Address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, and may be changed by the Representative Director upon lawful board approval and registration. 3. Banking Mandate. RESOLVED, that the Company's primary banking relationship shall be established with [Bank Name], Seoul Main Branch, and that the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer shall act as joint signatories; all transactions above the internal control threshold require dual authorization; and all factoring receipts and payments shall be routed through designated settlement accounts subject to anti-money laundering controls. 4. Statutory Officers and Corporate Governance. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Director and Chief Financial Officer; [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor; and [Name] is appointed Compliance and AML Officer for the purposes of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act and anti-money laundering regulation. Each officer shall hold office until the next annual meeting and is authorized to execute all registration forms, lease agreements, employment contracts, banking documents, and to affix the corporate seal. 5. General Authorization. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to do all acts and execute all documents necessary to register the Company, obtain the Business Registration Certificate, register the factoring business with the Financial Services Commission, file taxes, open settlement accounts, and carry out all post-registration filings required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (I-REG) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea and the local District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members shall first confirm that the proposed Korean legal name Yuhang Hoesa is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company by searching the Supreme Court online registration database. The incorporators shall then draft and execute the Articles of Incorporation, stating the object company business purpose to include accounts receivable factoring, purchase of receivables, reverse factoring, supply chain financing and related financial services; the registered office address; capital structure; member liability; and officer appointment provisions. Each member shall execute the Articles with an individual seal or formal signature and shall provide proof of identity. If a local agent is used, a power of attorney must be notarized and the agent must file its mandate with the Registry. The final executed Articles must be consistent with the business scope and the regulatory requirements for a specialized credit financial business.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate name search confirmation from I-REG
Draft Articles of Incorporation signed by all incorporators
Passport or national ID copy of each incorporator and appointed director
Notarized power of attorney in favor of the filing agent if applicable
Seal impression or signature specimen certificate
Registered office lease agreement or right-to-use document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search or filing is rejected because the proposed name is identical or similar to an existing company, select an alternate name, run a new search, amend the Articles accordingly, and resubmit the application; no substantive filing fee is forfeited beyond the incidental resubmission processing charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Contribution Account and Deposit of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed foreign-exchange bank in Seoul operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Commercial Act capital subscription rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Representative Director or authorized agent shall open a temporary corporate capital contribution bank account in the proposed registered corporate name at a Korean commercial bank. If capital is stated in the Articles, each incorporator shall remit the full subscribed contribution from a bank account held in the incorporator's own name; third-party deposits are not permitted. The bank shall issue a certificate of deposit or certificate of contribution reflecting the account name and exact amount. For non-resident investors, the inward remittance must be reported as a foreign direct investment where investment protection is sought, and a certificate of alien investment registration may be obtained from the delegated bank. The contributed funds remain blocked for withdrawal until the Court Registry confirms the incorporation registration, at which point the funds become available solely for lawful corporate purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation and corporate resolution authorizing bank account opening
Identification and proof of authority of all account signatories
Inward remittance advice and SWIFT confirmation for non-resident subscription funds
Court Registry name confirmation or pre-registration printout
Registered office lease agreement
Foreign investment notification form and alien investment registration documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remittance or foreign exchange reporting is queried, obtain a corrected beneficiary line in the SWIFT message matching the Yuhang Hoesa contribution account name and resubmit the foreign exchange report; no funds may be released until the bank and Court Registry confirm that the contribution is validly held.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration of Incorporation at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, or the district court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized applicant shall submit the application for commercial registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa to the Court Registry either physically or through the electronic I-REG system. Attach the executed Articles of Incorporation, certificate of contribution, identity documents, officer acceptance consents, registered office lease, and seal registration application. The Court examiner verifies the corporate name, object clauses, capital payment, statutory officer consents and the lawful business purpose. Upon approval, the Court assigns a corporate registration number and issues the Certificate of Company Registration and the Certificate of Registered Matters, which confer separate legal personality on Yuhang Hoesa. If the application is incomplete, the Registry issues a supplementary instruction requiring correction within the statutory cure period.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation using the official Commercial Registration Form
Executed Articles of Incorporation and notarization certificate if required by the Articles
Bank certificate of capital contribution deposit
Corporate seal registration application and seal certificate
Consent letters of the Representative Director, Directors, and Statutory Auditor accepting office
Identification and address proof for all directors and members
Proof of registered office lease and landlord consent
Power of attorney and identification of the registration agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Court Registry issues a supplementary instruction, cure the deficiency within the stated period by filing an amendment, corrected form, or additional evidence; if the application is rejected, correct the defects and refile a new application; an objection may also be filed through the Court Registry's non-contentious proceeding if the rejection is legally incorrect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and VAT Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service through the HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of the commercial registry date, the company shall file the business registration application with the District Tax Office or through the HomeTax electronic portal. The application must state the legal corporate name, corporate registration number, place of business, representative director, business purpose classification codes and settlement bank accounts. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate and assign a tax identification number. The company must also register for value-added tax under the Value-Added Tax Act and must comply with the general duties of a VAT taxpayer, including issuance of electronic tax invoices when service charges are collected. The entity must retain lease agreements, utility contracts, bank statements and employee records for tax inspection and corporate income tax compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration issued by the Court Registry
Lease agreement or free-use agreement for the business place
Representative Director identification and corporate seal or formal signature certificate
Corporate seal registration certificate
Bank account certificate from the capital contribution bank
Power of attorney if a tax agent is appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service returns the application due to discrepancies between the business purpose and the actual premises, amend the business registration form and lease evidence and resubmit; if the filing is late, submit a written explanation and request abatement of minor administrative penalties under the tax framework act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factoring Business Registration and AML Compliance under the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC), with examination performed by the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing any factoring, reverse factoring, trade receivables purchase or supply chain financing transaction, Yuhang Hoesa must apply to the Financial Services Commission for registration as a specialized credit financial business under Article 3(1) of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act. The application must include the Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Company Registration, opening balance sheet and bank balance certificate, evidence of paid-in capital and own capital satisfying the statutory minimum, a comprehensive business plan for trade receivables discounting, purchase and collection, a description of reverse-factoring payment rails using SWIFT wire and escrow settlement accounts, AML/CFT policies, the organizational chart, a compliance officer appointment letter, shareholding and beneficial ownership information, risk management rules and consumer data protection procedures. Factoring settlements must be structured so that payment is made to the designated corporate settlement account and not from customer deposits.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of specialized credit financial business limited to factoring
Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Company Registration
Opening balance sheet, paid-in capital certificate and bank balance certificate
Detailed factoring and reverse factoring business plan
AML/CFT policies, customer due diligence manual and transaction monitoring program
Organizational chart and compliance officer appointment letter
Corporate governance manual, internal accounting management rules and risk management rules
Beneficial ownership identification for all shareholders and directors
Lease agreement for the operational office
No prior tax or financial regulatory sanction declaration for substantial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC or FSS raises supplemental examination queries, the applicant shall provide a complete response within twenty business days; if the registration is denied, the company may correct the capital, governance, business plan or AML deficiencies and reapply, and it may use the FSS pre-consultation procedure before resubmission to prevent successive denials.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office Premises Fire Safety, Occupational Health Clearance and Final Post-Registration Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Fire Station under the National Fire Agency, District Building Administration, and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) with the Ministry of Employment and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because Yuhang Hoesa operates as a non-industrial financial services office and does not maintain any physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing facility, no Environmental Impact Assessment is triggered. However, the company must confirm that the leased office building holds a valid fire safety completion inspection certificate and must install fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation maps in each office area. The company shall apply for and receive a fire and civil defense inspection certificate for the premises. If the company employs five or more persons, it shall register for industrial accident compensation insurance with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service and appoint a workplace safety and health manager under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Annual fire drills and electrical safety checks should be completed and records retained for labor inspection.
required_dossiers: Building fire safety completion certificate from landlord
Fire inspection confirmation certificate from local fire station
Occupational accident compensation insurance registration certificate
Workplace safety and health manager appointment record
Electrical installation safety audit certificate if lease fit-out is modified
Employee lists and working rules for domestic employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies corrective deficiencies, complete the ordered repairs and schedule a reinspection; if KOSHA or the Ministry of Employment and Labor queries the workplace safety registration, promptly submit corrected employee counts and amended appointment records and obtain a confirmation certificate before the inspection deadline; no criminal penalty will apply if the defect is cured during the administrative correction period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the single electronic portal Home Tax Service (HTS) at https://www.hometax.go.kr; customs-related export and duty matters are administered by the Korea Customs Service as a separate authority reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 - Incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act and obtain the certified Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation from the registry court. STEP 2 - If the entity is foreign-invested, complete the Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank and obtain the Foreign Investment Report Certificate. STEP 3 - File the Business Registration Application (VAT/tax registration form) with the competent District Tax Office, either in person or via HTS. Attach: statutory business documents, the Foreign Investment Report Certificate, proof of the Korean place of business (lease agreement, ownership certificate), the foreign entity's constitutional documents, passport/ID and power of attorney of the foreign representative, and designation of a local tax manager or tax agent if applicable. STEP 4 - For a non-resident with no Korean place of business that is nevertheless required to be VAT-registered (e.g., electronic services supplier), submit the special Foreign Business VAT Registration through HTS and designate a Korean tax representative. STEP 5 - The District Tax Office examines the submission and issues the 10-digit Korean Business Registration Number (BRN), which is the statutory TIN for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the BRN appears on the Business Registration Certificate and must be displayed on all e-tax invoices. Issuance normally takes 3-5 working days for ordinary filings and longer if nominee/financial background verification is triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Korea has no check-the-box regime). A Yuhan Hoesa is per se a taxable corporation under Article 1-2 of the Corporate Tax Act, subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income when resident; no pass-through election is available. Hybrid-mismatch adjustments and entity classification for foreign tax purposes are mandatory under the Korean Act on Tax Adjustment of International Transactions, not elective. The only available elective group mechanism is the consolidated tax filing election for wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered by the NTS under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold applies for VAT registration in South Korea: every entrepreneur commencing a VAT-taxable business, including foreign non-resident vendors selling qualifying electronic services or using a Korean place of business, must register immediately. A simplified small-business facility exists on the computation side for sole proprietors whose annual taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000, but it does not remove the registration duty. For factoring and supply-chain financing, credit and financing transactions are generally VAT-exempt financial services while separately itemised management/factoring commission fees may be taxable, and once any taxable supply begins registration is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are the legal default for all VAT-registered businesses. Under Article 32 of the VAT Act, the seller must issue the e-tax invoice through the National Tax Service HTS system and transmit it to NTS in near-real-time, no later than one business day after issuance. Corporate ERP systems must integrate with the HTS e-tax invoice API using an accredited digital certificate and the 10-digit BRN; no proprietary API gateway is imposed, but the NTS Public Integrity Certification must be used. The HTS assigns a digitally signed serial/invoice identification number at issuance, and this HTS-certified transmission index is Korea's anti-fraud 'clearance stamp'. The buyer must also confirm the received e-tax invoice in HTS, allowing NTS to perform automated matching, detect missing or false invoices, and apply statutory surcharges retroactively.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exported tangible goods on the condition that the goods actually depart from Korea after being shipped under the Korean Customs Service export declaration and the exporter holds the evidence of export. Qualifying offshore digital and intangible services are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act when the service is supplied to a non-resident client and the use/benefit is deemed to take place outside Korea; the invoice must identify the foreign recipient, the foreign place of supply or offshore use, and the service nature. For the trade-finance/factoring scope, pure financing proceeds (interest, discount fees) are VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated, and any separately charged factoring or administration service rendered to a foreign counterparty for use outside Korea may qualify for zero-rating only with documentary proof of the foreign recipient and actual offshore benefit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Declaration of Goods / Export Shipment Report) endorsed for export in the exporter's name
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or equivalent carrier-issued transport document evidencing the physical departure of the goods from Korea

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by the Korean foreign-exchange bank evidencing receipt of the foreign settlement proceeds and matching the invoice, custom export declaration and shipping document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export zero-rating by cross-matching export declarations, e-tax invoices, shipping manifests, and banking records. If the export declaration, transport document, or FIRC is absent, incorrect, or inconsistent; if the 180-day inward remittance deadline is not met; or if the purported export is found to be a fake/round-tripping transaction, NTS will claw back any VAT refund already paid, assess the 10% VAT on the supply, impose an underreporting/reckless declaration surcharge (generally up to 40% of the unreported tax plus per-day statutory interest), and may refer the taxpayer to prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act for fraudulent zero-rating. The taxpayer bears the full burden of proof and must retain the complete export documentation package for at least five years from the reporting year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea, operating in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the Foreign Exchange Administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current account and capital account regime, yet requires strict reporting and verification through licensed foreign exchange banks. The Korean won is convertible for most genuine trading and investment purposes, but every cross-border receipt and payment must be routed through a domestic foreign exchange bank and must carry an accurate foreign exchange purpose classification. Capital account transactions such as equity infusions in the Yuhan Hoesa factoring entity, shareholder loans, and cross-border reverse factoring facilities are generally permitted but require ex post facto or prior reporting via the Foreign Exchange Information System, with threshold-based approvals enforced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Profit remittances and dividend outflows are accepted once corporate tax filings, audited financial statements, and capital verification reports are submitted, although banks may demand additional evidence of the underlying trade receivable portfolio and outstanding factoring obligations. Current account transactions, including factoring collections and settlement of assigned trade receivables, face minimal convertibility friction but must be traceable to bona fide cross-border trade contracts, tax invoices, and customs declarations. There is no overnight restriction that blocks lawful repatriation of profits, but Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration is required for foreign direct investment into the operational Korean entity, and all capital inflows must be received in a designated foreign exchange bank account before conversion into Korean won. The central bank and financial supervisory agencies monitor for round-tripping, phantom trade finance, and disguised cross-border lending; therefore, the factoring company must maintain a complete audit trail of underlying invoices, debtor acknowledgments, assignment notices, and proof of re-payment to foreign credit lines. Overall, convertibility is high for licensed commercial transactions, and the treasury structure can use standard SWIFT rails, KRW settlement through BOK-Wire+, and onshore deliverable forwards, provided that all required reports are filed on time.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters operating under the Korean foreign exchange regime are required to repatriate all export proceeds derived from Korean trade into South Korea, with a standard statutory collection window generally not exceeding the due date stated in the export contract or 90 days from the date of export clearance unless an extension is approved by the licensed foreign exchange bank. The mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign exchange receipts is essentially 100% in respect of repatriation: the proceeds must either be sold to a domestic foreign exchange bank or be credited into a proper foreign currency deposit account at such bank within the permitted period. Retention of export proceeds offshore without a licensed bank arrangement is not permitted for a resident Korean legal entity. The Yuhan Hoesa factoring operation, when financing Korean export receivables, must therefore ensure that each factored export invoice is supported by customs declarations, e-tax invoices, bills of lading, and a remedial duty to surrender all related collections through the designated Korean foreign exchange bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions are not viable as primary banking or treasury rails for a licensed South Korean factoring entity. South Korea requires any entity handling domestic KRW settlement, escrow, or payment products to obtain authorization under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and related Financial Services Commission supervision. Most foreign EMIs and neobanks do not hold a Korean EFT license, cannot establish direct participation in Korea's interbank clearing systems, and are not formally recognized as foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Consequently, relying on a cross-border EMI for aggregation of export factoring proceeds, capital injection verification, or outbound trade disbursements would create severe KYC and reconciliation exposure. The EMI route may be used only as an auxiliary, non-escrow channel for small foreign-currency receivables from remote digital content markets, but all operational liquidity, capital verification, and statutory FX reporting must remain with a regulated Korean foreign exchange bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks generally require at least one authorized signatory and, in most robust compliance models, a statutory director or representative to appear physically in-branch during corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is possible in limited circumstances through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, but leading tier-1 banks will typically insist on an in-person interview when the entity is an offshore-owned factoring company with medium-risk trade finance exposure. The interviewer must verify real-name identity under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, confirm the company's business purpose, examine the certified Korean articles of incorporation, and validate the operator's actual managerial authority. A physical presence on the ground, either through the nominee director or through an authorized on-site financial officer, is strongly recommended to expedite account opening, capital escrow, and foreign exchange dealing limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore UBO complexity involving nominee shareholders or cross-border holding layers routed through shell jurisdictions, which may obscure the ultimate beneficiary of the Yuhan Hoesa factoring operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of members and shareholders, full corporate organizational chart through every intermediary layer, notarized passport and resident registration copies for each ultimate beneficial owner, bank-issued source of wealth statements, and corporate registry abstracts from each jurisdiction accompanied by apostille or consular legalization where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of disguised loan trafficking or unlicensed money lending because the factoring company receives foreign capital injections and distributes funds against assigned receivables in a manner that could be classified as consumer or shadow lending rather than commercial or reverse factoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory factoring or trade finance license certificate from the relevant Korean financial supervisory authority, executed master factoring agreements, entity-to-entity assignment agreements, debtor acceptance notices, underlying export and import contracts, a schedule of receivables showing all advances and discount fees, audited financial statements, and evidence that funding is deployed strictly to qualified commercial invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice duplication, fictitious trade receivables, or round-tripping red flags arising from cross-border trade supply chain factoring, where the same underlying goods or invoices could be financed twice by Korean and foreign credit providers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: National Tax Service e-tax invoice copies, customs declaration matching receipts, bills of lading, airway bills or transport documents, debtor-side accounts payable ledgers, independent factual confirmation letters from obligated debtors, publicly verifiable invoice reference numbers, and a controlled single-credit-rails declaration confirming that each receivable is financed through only one senior lender.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed persons, or adverse media exposure of the counterparties, underlying trade obligors, or managers of the factoring company, particularly where the trade finance portfolio spans high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live sanctions screening reports spanning UN, OFAC, EU, and Korean government lists, transactional screening logs for all debtors and suppliers, negative news and PEP search results, sworn beneficial ownership questionnaires, evidence of no tax evasion or customs undervaluation, and a detailed corporate compliance policy approved by the board of directors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Yuhan Hoesa factoring entity must be structured as either foreign direct investment registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act or as a foreign currency loan reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The remitting entity must use a standard SWIFT MT103 message routed through a qualified intermediary to a designated Korean tier-1 foreign exchange bank, with the beneficiary account clearly identified as the capital escrow account or foreign currency demand deposit account of the Korean LLC. The bank will require the remitter to include a compliant foreign exchange purpose code, typically the classification corresponding to equity participation, foreign currency borrowing, or trade finance credit line injection, along with the exact Korean entity registration number and bank-provided reference for capital verification. The Korean receiving bank will issue a capital verification certificate where applicable, and the treasury must deposit the proceeds in the designated escrow account before conversion into Korean won at the market exchange rate. Any future disbursement from the escrow account must follow the original purpose schedule and must be matched against underlying factoring contracts, invoices, and funding plans to satisfy the Financial Services Commission and Bank of Korea audit expectations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should run through SWIFT MT103 for direct trade payments and factoring advance remittances, with the domestic KRW leg executed through BOK-Wire+ for high-value instructions or through Korean Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute rails for smaller settlement. Commercial letters of credit should be issued through the Korean issuing bank using confirmed SWIFT MT700/MT707 messaging, while documentary collections may be presented under SWIFT MT761 or standard ICC collection instructions. The factoring treasury must maintain strict segregation between the purchase price paid to the assigning exporter and the final collection proceeds received from the foreign debtor; each outbound payment needs a supporting trade contract, invoice, assignment notice, tax invoice, customs declaration, and bank-compliant purpose code. The bank will require that underlying receivable financing is not disguised salary remittance or portfolio diversification, and that all disbursements match the commercial invoice values and maturity dates recorded in the factoring system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts against actual trade receivables or payables
FX swaps for liquidity transformation between Korean won and the financing currency, limited to matched tenors and underlying trade settlement exposure
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term offshore credit line hedging, provided the swap transactions are supported by the underlying factoring facility agreements

Onshore non-deliverable forwards used with caution and only through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank for non-deliverable KRW exposure management, subject to underlying trade documentation and bank reporting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with financial statements and reconciled Factoring Reserve and Loss Allowance schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the Seoul District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the close of each calendar fiscal year; one-month extension to 30 April if the return is prepared by a licensed tax accountant (sesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or underreported corporate tax attracts an additional 20% negligent filing penalty (40% if intentionally false), unpaid tax accrues 0.025% daily late-payment interest, and sustained arrears can trigger asset seizure, bank account garnishment, and a court-administered dissolution request after one year of ceased operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (external audit disclosure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART electronic disclosure; shareholder confirmation at the annual members' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Members' meeting must be convened no later than 31 March after fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be filed on DART within two weeks after approval, and in ordinary calendar-year cases no later than 15 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of a registered CPA auditor or omission of the audit report is a regulatory offense with pecuniary fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; FSS may impose a reinvestigation order, suspend the factoring license for a repeat default, or refer the company to prosecution for making a false audit statement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Factoring Portfolio Compliance Return for the licensed trade-finance factoring business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) EDIF reporting platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March each year, covering the preceding fiscal year's on-balance-sheet factoring assets, cross-border reverse factoring volumes, SWIFT settlement activity, AML/CFT CDD exceptions, and net capital maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or material misstatement may lead to a daily administrative fine, suspension or revocation of the ISIC 6492 factoring license, and disqualification of officers; continued default after three months is treated as an insolvency risk event and triggers financial-stability review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual member register confirmation, contribution transfer log, and charge register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry and Korean Court Registrar (inspection rights); registered office files subject to court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At all times current; as of each annual members' meeting held by 31 March the registers must reflect all contribution transfers recorded within 15 calendar days of any transfer or encumbrance event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unrecorded transfer is ineffective against the company and third parties; the company and responsible officers may be fined for failure to produce registers when ordered by a court or FSS, and a defective register can be cited as a governance deficiency in the FSC license renewal review.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent CPA audit is legally required for this Yuhan Hoesa if any of the following is met at fiscal year-end: (1) total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.4 million); (2) total assets equal or exceed KRW 3 billion (approx. USD 2.2 million) and annual revenue equal or exceed KRW 10 billion; (3) total assets equal or exceed KRW 3 billion and the average workforce equals or exceeds 100 full-time employees; or (4) the entity is unable to claim a small-company exemption because it is a licensed cross-border factoring and institutional lender subject to FSC audit covenants. The licensing condition alone makes the annual audit unavoidable for the trade finance portfolio.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for all audited Yuhan Hoesa entities; non-audited small companies may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or the SME Accounting Standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; the financial statements must be kept in KRW and the statutory audit opinion must be issued by a Korean certifying CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: As a licensed factoring company subject to Korean AML/CFT regulation, the Yuhan Hoesa must perform annual beneficial-ownership confirmation for its counterparties and borrowers, and re-identify its own members and UBOs at least once every 12 months. Any transfer of a member's contribution requires a joint transferor and transferee application to record the change in the company's member register, and the updated register must be signed and maintained at the registered office before the change can be asserted against the company. A 30-day reporting window applies to changes in qualifying foreign-invested shareholding where foreign-ownership filings are required; otherwise the register is continuously updated.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive 9% to 24%; top marginal tax rate of 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 50 billion (brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 10 billion, 21% from KRW 10 billion to KRW 50 billion, 24% above KRW 50 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone (FEZ) incentives under Foreign Investment Promotion Act Art. 121-2 grant 50% to 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years and a further 50% exemption for the following 2 years for eligible foreign-invested high-technology ventures; general R&D tax credits of 20-40% are available under Special Taxation Control Act; job-creation/increase tax credits apply for new hires; no patent-box or factoring-specific incentive regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Standard Form 63-100) under Corporate Tax Act Art. 60 and Enforcement Decree Art. 97; filed electronically through the HomeTax/UTAX e-filing portal of the National Tax Service (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a semi-annual interim corporate tax return for the first half of the fiscal year must also be filed within 2 months after the end of that first half-year, and two prepayment instalments are due during the fiscal year when prior-year corporate tax exceeds KRW 10 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year corporation, the statutory deadline is 31 March. Extension is available for up to one month where the return is prepared or reviewed by an independent CPA, and up to two additional months may be granted by the NTS Commissioner for consolidated groups or foreign-affiliated subsidiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name (Yuhan Hoesa), business registration number, head office address, representative director's ID number, and business-type classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare that Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean resident domestic corporation within the meaning of Article 2 of the Corporate Tax Act. Attach Schedule 60-13 of non-resident shareholder information and, if any foreign holding company maintains a Korean fixed place of business through Yuhan Hoesa, disclose that branch/Permanent Establishment so that domestic return obligations are not accidentally duplicated or omitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating income from factoring commissions, reverse-factoring discounts, receivables purchase spreads, interest income, and other fees; less direct finance costs, commissions, and brokerage expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose revenue generated from non-resident obligors and any invoice in which the counterparty is a non-resident related party. If the aggregate cross-border factoring-related transaction with a single related counterparty exceeds KRW 5 billion, the additional transfer pricing local file reconciliation must be attached to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory disallowances for entertainment expenses, special bad-debt reserves, unprovisioned unrealised exchange losses, related-party excess interest, and any non-business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Re-add interest, royalties, and management fees paid to a foreign related party that fail the 30% interest barrier rule or the utility/arm's-length substance test under the International Tax Adjustment Act. A deduction for a foreign service fee is allowed only if actual services were rendered and are evidenced by contemporaneous contracts, invoices and work papers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base computed after net operating loss carryforwards, tax-exempt income, charitable deduction limits, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating losses may be carried forward for 10 years for tax years beginning on or after 2020; for prior-year losses, the 5-year limitation still applies. Foreign-source factoring losses are deductible only against foreign-source income in accordance with the Worldwide Taxation rules unless the treaty permits a Korean mechanism for foreign-source loss recognition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the tentative corporate income tax by applying the progressive 9/19/21/24 percent brackets to the taxable base and then applying exemptions, credits and the foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where Yuhan Hoesa earns factoring fees from foreign debtors, a foreign tax credit is available for foreign withholding tax and income tax paid overseas if the tax is 'foreign corporation tax' under Article 57 of the Corporate Tax Act. Attach proof of foreign tax payment and translated copies; treaty relief against Korean source dividends, interest or royalties requires a valid Tax Residency Certificate, not merely a nil domestic tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement enumerating cross-border related-party transactions: factoring receivable transfers, discount interest, management fees, royalties, guarantees, and loans with each non-resident related party; transfer pricing method used; and arm's-length price determination details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions with a specific counterparty equal or exceed KRW 5 billion. State the selected pricing methodology (P, RP, CP, TNMM, or Profit Split), provide justification based on a contemporaneous comparability analysis, and disclose the Korean entity's roles, risks and assets. Failure to submit this schedule is an independent non-filing penalty trigger.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under Article 76 of the Corporate Tax Act (increased to 35% when the omission is fraudulent); unfaithful or understated reporting triggers a 10% (or 20% for concealment) penalty of the understated tax. Late payment interest accrues under Article 21 of the National Tax Collection Act at 3% of the overdue element plus 0.0225% per day until paid. Intentional tax evasion is criminally punished under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act: imprisonment of up to 2 years and fines up to five times the evaded amount; aggravated penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment apply for substantial evasion schemes.
